problems.comment:
The wind slabs of the last few days are in some cases still prone to triggering. Single winter sport participants can release avalanches in some places, including medium-sized ones. 
 Backcountry touring calls for careful route selection.
On grassy slopes numerous small and, in isolated cases, medium-sized gliding avalanches are to be expected. Caution is to be exercised in areas with glide cracks.

bulletin.snowpack: Snow depths are above average for the time of year. Weak layers prone to triggering are present mainly in the new and wind-drifted snow layers of the last few days. These are stabilizing rapidly. Pronounced, faceted weak layers are scarcely present.
bulletin.tendency:
Dry avalanches
Individual avalanche prone locations for dry avalanches are to be found in particular on very steep slopes. Apart from the danger of being buried, restraint should be exercised as well in view of the danger of avalanches sweeping people along and giving rise to falls.
Wet-snow avalanches
Gliding avalanches are possible at any time. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided as far as possible.

problems.comment: On steep grassy slopes numerous gliding avalanches are to be expected, even large ones. Areas with glide cracks are to be avoided.
The fresh and somewhat older wind slabs are in some cases prone to triggering. Mostly avalanches are medium-sized. Backcountry touring calls for careful route selection.

bulletin.snowpack:
The snow depths at elevated altitudes are far above average for the time of year. Weak layers prone to triggering are found mainly in the sometimes thick layers of new and wind-drifted snow from the last few days. These are stabilizing rapidly.
Above approximately 2600 m, on north- and east-facing slopes, there is in places still coarse-grained old snow at the snow base. This old snow close to the ground is now overlain so thickly that fractures in layers of the snowpack close to the ground are not very likely.
